not_eligible_because: one solver over one simulator board: which placement lost the Perfect Clear has no second implementation
rule: a placement miss: a PC was possible before the lock (hindsight, the round's dealt sequence, frame <= 6 rows) and not after it (re-checked with the engine's own movegen, 180 included), the lock did not itself perfect-clear and the next lock brought no garbage. Reported when in_preview (a PC existed using only the current piece, the hold and the 5-piece preview) and verified (the next lock is inside the verified prefix).
dpc_rule: a DPC miss: a placement miss inside a pc window (the locks after a Perfect Clear), reported in HINDSIGHT (the PC used pieces the preview had not shown yet; in_preview says when it did not need to) when verified_resumed: the next lock is inside the verified prefix re-walked with one tolerance, a Perfect Clear the engine sends as one attack matching the game's packets at that frame when they sum to it (the game sends the clear and its All Clear bonus apart). verified_resumed_to is that walk's last lock; without the tolerance the walk reproduces verified_to on every player.

categories.hole: the placement covered an empty cell
categories.over: the stack after the placement is taller than the frame of the solver's PC
categories.hold: the solver's first piece is not the piece placed
categories.spot: the same piece, placed somewhere else

caveat: a PC being possible does not mean the player was building one
